Reserved On : 03.06.2025 vs State Of Himachal Pradesh on 6
June, 2025
Author: Virender Singh

Bench: Virender Singh
2025:Hhc:17993 In The High Court Of Himachal Pradesh, Shimla.

sentences.text: Cr. Mp (M) No. : 1138 of 2025

Reserved on : 03.06.2025
 Decided on : 06.06.2025
Rajinder Kumar ...Applicant
 Versus
State of Himachal Pradesh ...Respondent

Coram
The Hon'ble Mr. Justice Virender Singh, Judge.

Whether approved for reporting?1 For the applicant : Mr. N.S. Chandel, Senior Advocate with Mr. Sidharth, Advocate.
For the respondent : Mr. Tejasvi Sharma & Mr. H.S. Rawat, Additional Advocated General with Mr.
Rohit Sharma, Deputy Advocate General, assisted by ASI Pawan Kumar, Police Station Shahpur,
District Kangra, H.P. Respondent No.2, joined the proceedings through Video Conferencing.

Virender Singh, Judge ApplicantRajinder Kumar has filed the present application, under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (hereinafter referred to as the 'BNSS'), with a prayer to release him on bail, during the Whether Reporters of local papers may be allowed to see the judgment?

Yes. 
2 2025:HHC:17993 pendency of trial, in case arising out of FIR No.36 of 2024, dated 26.03.2024,
registered, under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code, (hereinafter referred to as the 'IPC'), with Police Station, Shahpur, District Kangra, H.P.
2.
According to the applicant, he is innocent person and has falsely been implicated by the Police, in the present case.
According to him, he has no concern with the crime, for which, he has been arrested by the Police.

3. It is the further case of the applicant that the investigation, in the present case, is complete and the police has filed the chargesheet, which is pending adjudication in the competent Court of law.
Reserved On : 03.06.2025 vs State Of Himachal Pradesh on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78925344/

1 5. Applicant has tried his luck by moving similar application before learned Additional Sessions JudgeI, Kangra at Dharamshala, District Kangra, however, his application has been dismissed vide order dated 20.06.2024.
6. Thereafter, the applicant has filed Cr.MP(M) No. 1420 of 2024, before this Court, which was dismissed on 11.09.2024.
Thereafter, the applicant has again filed 3 2025:HHC:17993 similar application, bearing Cr.MP(M) No.2338 of 2024, before this Court, which was dismissed as withdrawn.
7. It is the further case of the applicant that his custodial interrogation is no longer required by the Police.
As such, no useful purpose would be served by keeping him in the judicial custody.

8. On the basis of the above facts, Mr. N.S. Chandel, learned Senior Advocate assisted by Mr.
Sidharth, Advocate has given certain undertakings, on behalf of the applicant, to which, the applicant is ready to abide by, in case, the applicant is ordered to be released on bail.
9. On the basis of the above facts, a prayer has been made to allow the application.

10. When put to notice, the police has filed the status report, disclosing therein that on 26.03.2024,
the prosecutrix/respondent No.2, along with her friend appeared before the Police and made a complaint that she is resident of the address, as mentioned in the application.

10.1. In December,
2022, she had enrolled herself for PHD in Chemistry, in CUHP 'X'.
Dr. Rajender Kumar 4 2025:HHC:17993 (applicant) was her supervisor.
At that time, he was Head of Department in Chemistry Department.

It is her further case that applicant used to talk to her in the normal way for the initial six months and when she requested her to provide the topic for research, then, the applicant had put off the matter on one pretext or the other.
The said topic was not finalized by the applicant till the end of 2022, whereas, according to her, other students had started working on the topic given by the applicant.

10.2. It is the further case of the complainant that in the year 2022, the applicant allegedly stated that the prosecutrix is roaming with the boys, due to this fact, the prosecutrix suffered mental trauma.
Thereafter, he has selected the topic for her, for which, he has also suggested the software.
10.3. As per the further version of the complainant, on the repeated demand, the said software was provided to her, but, the applicant has not guided her properly and tortured her mentally.

Applicant has also threatened her to stop her fellowship on 25.03.2024.
5 2025:HHC:17993 10.4.
According to the complainant, she had approached the applicant in order to clear her doubt, upon which, he has told to change the topic and also assure that he will do whatever, she wants.
In the evening time, applicant called her to University Gate to discuss the matter.
Consequently, she had gone there.

10.5. Thereafter, the applicant asked the complainant to discuss the matter by sitting somewhere and he insisted her to go to Gopal Restaurant, where, the applicant had booked a room and disclosed the prosecutrix that they will discuss the topic there and will have their dinner there.
In the room, the applicant allegedly raped her twice.
10.6. Applicant took the prosecutrix to Gopal Restaurant at about 7.30 p.m. and they came back at 10.00 p.m.

She Reserved On : 03.06.2025 vs State Of Himachal Pradesh on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78925344/
2 has prayed that action be taken against the accused.

sentences.text: 11. On the basis of the above facts, the FIR, in question, was registered and the criminal machinery swung into motion.

12. Thereafter, the prosecutrix was medicolegally examined, on 26.03.2024 and the physical evidence, so 6 2025:HHC:17993 collected by the doctor, and the final opinion was deferred till the receipt of RFSL report.
Applicant was arrested on 27.03.2025.
He was also medicolegally examined.
13. During investigation, the statement of the prosecutrix was recorded, under Section 164 Cr.PC.
The vehicle used in the alleged crime was also taken into possession.
It is the further case of the police that although, three cases were found to be registered against the applicant, but, he has been acquitted in all the cases.
14. After receipt of FSL report, and on completion of the investigation, the police has filed the charge sheet, in the competent Court of law.
Thereafter, the competent Court of law has taken cognizance and out of 36 witnesses, 12 witnesses have already been examined.

15. On the basis of the above facts, it has been argued by Mr. Tejasvi Sharma, learned Additional Advocate General that in view of the presumption, which is in favour of the prosecution, under Section 114A of the Indian Evidence Act, the applicant is not entitled for bail, as he has committed a heinous offence.
7 2025:HHC:17993 16.

No doubt the relationship between the prosecutrix and applicant was teacher and student, which is pious relationship, but, merely on the basis of the above relationship, the petitioner cannot be kept in judicial custody, that too, for indefinite period.

17. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Criminal Appeal No.2787 of 2024, titled as Javed Gulam Nabi Shaikh versus State of Maharashtra and Another, has held that accused is presumed to be innocent until proven guilty.

entities.text: Javed Gulam Nabi Shaikh versus State of Maharashtra and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Relevant paragraphs 18 to 20, of the judgment, are reproduced, as under: "18 Criminals are not born out but made.
The human potential in everyone is good and so, never write off any criminal as beyond redemption.
This humanist fundamental is often missed when dealing with delinquents, juvenile and adult.
Indeed, every saint has a past and every sinner a future.
When a crime is committed, a variety of factors is responsible for making the offender commit the crime.

Those factors may be social and economic, may be, the result of value erosion or parental neglect;
may be, because of the stress of circumstances, or the manifestation of temptations in a milieu of affluence contrasted with indigence or other privations.

19 If the State or any prosecuting agency including the court concerned has no wherewithal to provide or protect the fundamental right of an applicant to have a speedy trial as enshrined under Article 21 of the 8 2025:HHC:17993 Constitution then the State or any other prosecuting agency Reserved On : 03.06.2025 vs State Of Himachal Pradesh on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78925344/
3 should not oppose the plea for bail on the ground that the crime committed is serious.
Article 21 of the Constitution applies irrespective of the nature of the crime.
20 We may hasten to add that the petitioner is still an accused; not a convict.

The overarching postulate of criminal jurisprudence that an applicant is presumed to be innocent until proven guilty cannot be brushed aside lightly,
howsoever stringent the penal law may be."

18. So far as the arguments of the learned Additional Advocate General, qua the presumption, under Section 114A of the Indian Evidence Act, is concerned, to the considered opinion of this Court, as this stage, the prosecution cannot derive the benefit from the said provisions, as the said provisions comes into play, once, the prosecutrix proves the fact that applicant had committed the rape.

In other words, the said presumption would be taken into consideration, at an appropriate stage, i.e.,
when the prosecution will prove the allegations of rape.
19. The applicant is permanent resident of Himachal Pradesh, as such, it cannot be apprehended that in case, he is released on bail, he may not be available for trial.
20. Moreover, keeping in view the pace of trial, the chances of conclusion of trial against the applicant are not 9 2025:HHC:17993 so bright.

As such, no useful purpose would be served by keeping the applicant in the judicial custody, that too, for indefinite period.
21.
In this case, the prosecutrix has joined the proceedings through Video Conferencing and prayed that the bail may not be given to the applicant and in case, he is released on bail, he may coerce her.
22. So far as the said apprehension is concerned, to the considered opinion of this Court, for that reasonable condition can be imposed, in case he is ordered to be released on bail.

23. At the time of deciding the bail application, detailed discussion of the evidence, so collected, by the prosecution or about the defence, which has been taken, by the applicant, should be avoided, as,
it would cause prejudice to the case of the prosecution, as well as, to that of the accused.
24.

The bail application cannot be rejected, as a matter of punishment, as, pretrial punishment is prohibited under the law and punishment can only be imposed, after the full fledged trial, by competent Court of 10 2025:HHC:17993 law.
The applicant is presumed to be innocent, until proven guilty.
25. Considering all these facts, this Court is of the view that the bail application is liable to be allowed and is accordingly allowed.

The applicant is ordered to be released on bail in case FIR No.36 of 2024, dated 26.03.2024, registered, under Section 376 of the IPC with Police Station, Shahpur,
District Kangra, H.P., on his furnishing personal bonds, in the sum of Rs.50,000/, with two sureties, each, in the like amount, to the satisfaction of learned trial Court.

Any of the observations made herein above shall not be taken as an expression of opinion on the merits of the case as these observations are confined only to the disposal of the present bail application.
28. It is made clear that the respondentState is at liberty to move an appropriate application, in case, any of the bail conditions is found to be violated by the applicant.

29. The Registry is directed to forward a soft copy of the bail order to the Superintendent of Jail,
Lala Lajpat Rai Open Air Correctional Home, Dharamshala, District Kangra, through email, with a direction to enter the date of grant of bail in the eprison software.

30. In case, the applicant is not released within a period of seven days from the date of grant of bail,
the Superintendent of Jail, Lala Lajpat Rai Open Air Correctional Home, Dharamshala, District Kangra, is directed to inform this fact to the Secretary, DLSA, Kangra at Dharamshala.

entities.text: Lala Lajpat Rai Open Air Correctional Home, Dharamshala
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
The Superintendent of Jail, Lala Lajpat Rai Open Air Correctional Home, Dharamshala, District Kangra,
is further directed that if the applicant fails to furnish the bail bonds, as per the order passed by this 12 2025:HHC:17993 Court, within a period of one month from today, then, the said fact be submitted to this Court.
( Virender Singh ) Judge June 05, 2025(ps)
